title: Advanced Emergency Braking System (AEBS) for light vehicles (version 2.5.0)
scope_summary: Approves vehicle types with regard to an on-board Advanced Emergency Braking System that avoids or mitigates rear-end in-lane collisions with a passenger car, impacts with a pedestrian and impacts with a bicycle. It applies to M1 and N1 vehicles, and offers an alternative to UN R131 for M2 vehicles and for M3/N2 vehicles of 8 t or less maximum weight with hydraulic braking.
scope_quote: This Regulation applies to the approval of vehicles of Category M1 and N1 with regard to an on-board system to (a) Avoid or mitigate the severity of a rear-end in lane collision with a passenger car, (b) Avoid or mitigate the severity of an impact with a pedestrian. (c) Avoid or mitigate the severity of an impact with a bicycle. ... This Regulation also offers an alternative set of requirements for vehicles of Category M2, and for those of Categories M3/N2 with a maximum weight below or equal to 8 tons, equipped with hydraulic braking, to those contained in UN Regulation No. 131.
vehicle_categories: M3 with maximum weight <= 8 t and hydraulic braking (alternative to UN R131)
N2 with maximum weight <= 8 t and hydraulic braking (alternative to UN R131)
applies_to_components: Emergency braking demand to the service braking system
AEBS warning indication / failure warning signal
Electronic control system of the AEBS (Annex 3 complex electronic systems)
Driver interruption / override of the system
relation_to_other_regulations: Alternative to UN Regulation No. 131 for M2, and for M3/N2 with maximum weight <= 8 t and hydraulic braking; Contracting Parties applying both recognise approvals to either regulation as equally valid
Refers to UN Regulation No. 13-H (Annex 6, Appendix 2 k-test method) for determining the sufficient nominal Peak Braking Coefficient
Refers to UN Regulation No. 13 (Annex 13, Appendix 2 k-test method) for determining the Peak Braking Coefficient permitting the design maximum deceleration
Vehicle categories as defined in the Consolidated Resolution R.E.3 (ECE/TRANS/WP.29/78/Rev.6)
'If-fitted' regulation: it does not prevent Contracting Parties from mandating the fitting of AEBS approved to it

defined_terms.label: Advanced Emergency Braking System (AEBS)
defined_terms.definition: A system which can automatically detect an imminent forward collision and activate the vehicle braking system to decelerate the vehicle with the purpose of avoiding or mitigating a collision.

defined_terms.label: Emergency Braking
defined_terms.definition: A braking demand emitted by the AEBS to the service braking system of the vehicle.

defined_terms.label: Collision Warning
defined_terms.definition: A warning emitted by the AEBS to the driver when the AEBS has detected an imminent forward collision.

defined_terms.label: Vehicle Type with Regard to its Advanced Emergency Braking System
defined_terms.definition: A category of vehicles which do not differ in vehicle features significantly influencing AEBS performance or in the type and design of the AEBS.

defined_terms.label: Soft Target
defined_terms.definition: A target that will suffer minimum damage and cause minimum damage to the subject vehicle in the event of a collision.

defined_terms.label: Vehicle Target
defined_terms.definition: A target that represents a vehicle.

defined_terms.label: Pedestrian Target
defined_terms.definition: A soft target that represents a pedestrian.

defined_terms.label: Bicycle Target
defined_terms.definition: A soft target that represents a bicycle with cyclist.

defined_terms.label: Common Space
defined_terms.definition: An area on which two or more information functions (e.g. symbol) may be displayed, but not simultaneously.

defined_terms.label: Self-Check
defined_terms.definition: An integrated function that checks for a system failure on a continuous basis at least while the system is active.

defined_terms.label: Time To Collision (TTC)
defined_terms.definition: The longitudinal distance between the subject vehicle and the target divided by their longitudinal relative speed, at any instant in time.

defined_terms.label: Dry road affording good adhesion
defined_terms.definition: A road with a sufficient nominal Peak Braking Coefficient permitting a mean fully developed deceleration of at least 9 m/s2 or the vehicle's design maximum deceleration, whichever is lower.

defined_terms.label: Initialisation
defined_terms.definition: The process of setting-up the operation of the system after switching ON the vehicle until it is fully functioning.

defined_terms.label: The System
defined_terms.definition: An electronic control system (or complex electronic control system) providing or forming part of the AEBS function, subject to Annex 3 documentation and safety-concept requirements.

applicability_hints: Vehicle-level approval: AEBS components (forward-looking radar, camera, lidar, ECU, brake actuation interface) are not approved separately but are assessed as part of the vehicle's AEBS type
Any change to sensors, AEBS software or vehicle features that significantly influence AEBS performance may change the vehicle type and require extension (section 7)
The AEBS electronic control system falls under Annex 3 complex electronic systems requirements (documentation, safety concept, fault strategy)
Driver HMI elements (collision warning, failure/deactivation telltales, deactivation switch) are covered by 5.4/5.5
Heavier hydraulic-braked M2, M3 and N2 vehicles (<= 8 t) can be approved to R152 instead of R131
'If-fitted' regulation: applies when the vehicle is equipped with an AEBS for which approval is sought, though Contracting Parties may mandate it
Separate approval scopes exist for car-to-car, pedestrian and bicycle scenarios; a system addressing vulnerable road users is tested with pedestrian/bicycle soft targets
PTI provisions (5.6) require the AEBS operational status to be verifiable, affecting diagnostic interfaces
Virtual testing (6.11/Annex 4) can be used for dynamic tests, bringing simulation toolchains into scope of assessment
